(4) It is great for removing eye makeup, without eye irritation. (5) I have VERY sensitive skin. I use prescription tretinoin (retinoid) which makes my skin dry & sensitive to most products. My skin often stings when applying moisturizers or cleansers. This balm is actually soooo soothing and calms my skin: no stinging, no burning, no irritation.  BOTTOM-LINE: This is a cost-effective, scent-free cleansing balm which is safe for use around your eyes. It is calming to most skin-types & an effective cleanser. It is definitely worth a try! Now the presence of coconut oil likely won?™t be a problem if you only plan to use this on your body, but it can be a big problem on your face which is where there are more sebaceous glands prone to inflammation and breakouts. I realize some people don?™t get bad reactions from using comedogenic ingredients on their face, but they are the minority and not the majority. Coconut oil, despite its many wonderful benefits to skin and hair, is just unfortunately a known comedogenic ingredient. For this reason I never recommend people apply coconut oil on the face, but body and hair should be fine for most people. If you are experiencing breakouts with this product, which I see many reviewers complaining about, now you likely know the reason why.As a body product, this is definitely worth checking out, but I would strongly advise applying this on your face if you have sensitive skin or are prone to breakouts. You may want to find another product that is non-comedogenic and better formulated for the face.

I?™ve tried this all over my body (applying different days for different sections) and I?™m so so impressed! I love the smell and simple application as well as how EASY it is to build. I didn?™t get crazy results the first use on my upper body and went for a second application the next night. They did awesome! I did two separate applications on my lower body (all between showers) and my overall tan looks great. I will not, not use these ever.

Not sure how I missed the boat on these tanning drops, but I?™m back on!  These drops are super easy to use (no mitt, etc.) after exfoliating and application, you can see yourself get tan by the minute.

I ended up having blotches around my joint areas. Different lighting shows your self tan differently. This was my first time using this product. It was darker in certain areas and was lighter in others, but I used the same amount of drops with every pump of lotion. I?™m not sure if it had something to do with what the mixing ratio for the amount of lotion you use with the amount of drops, but if this company would?™ve been more specific or provided a guide it would?™ve been more helpful. The areas that were noticeably darker were my wrists, my ankles, knees, and neck. Fluorescent lighting versus warm lighting also shows a difference in your blending too. Warm lighting it looked blended but once I stepped out into the day time you could see all of my mistakes. EVEN after all of my lotion had been rubbed in completely the day before.

This stuff is next-level. I HATE self tanning. I always get streaks, the smell is awful, it takes forever to dry, etc. etc. But this is AMAZING. I put ~10 drops in my lotion per section of my body (1 leg, stomach, etc.). It is so easy to apply, doesn?™t leave streaks, and doesn?™t smell at all!

I?™ve only use this product once so far. I am already really pleased with the results! The bottle says to use 1-12 drops mixed in your moisturizer. I did this last night, with only 3 drops added to my moisturizer! Already noticed results this morning! My skin didn?™t feel oily or sticky or anything, just felt like any other night with just using my moisturizer.

I am super fair and I have tried basically every tanning product on the market. This smells great, works fast and didn?™t make me break out! I?™d say the color developed in about 4 hours. I?™ve only used it on my face, I feel like you?™d have to use quite a bit for body so I?™d rather save it up. Also only used 2 drops and it?™s perfect color!

I tried this one and it wasn?™t worth the purchase. I mixed about 6 ish drops into my moisturizer and was diligent about rubbing it in everywhere because I was scared of it streaking. I?™m gonna try this again and be more conscious of touching my face, but this isn?™t a good sign to me. For my other self tanners I?™d usually apply them before bed so I could wake up with a glow, and I don?™t feel comfortable doing that with this one.

I am super pale but I self-tan, I was looking for a better way to get my face to have a nice glow to it as well. I decided to purchase the light shade but easily could have done medium as well. column11: uneven tan.  and it smells not so nice

works rly good!! i put about 2 drops in pump of moisturizer, and put on my face & neck :)) also, last a veryyyyy long time!!!!!!

column11: It for sure works! Read for more details..

column10: I was super pleasantly surprised by this, especially after reading some of the negative reviews. For the past few years I?™ve used the st. tropez express self tan mousse but I fly a lot to and from college so this seems more convenient/less messy to pack. I was pretty conservative with how much I put on my first time (2 drops into moisturizer for face+neck, about 2 for each arm and about 6 for each leg/butt all mixed into a LOT of lotion). I put it on in the middle of the day yesterday and didn?™t notice a huge difference until this morning. I have a nice bronzy glow that looks about the same as leaving on the st tropez express mousse for 2 hours. I?™m not noticing any self-tanner smell today but it was pretty strong yesterday. I really like that it?™s meant to be mixed into moisturizer because I hate feeling of how dry my skin is when I have to skip lotion and put on a mousse. I was excited and used 6 drops my first time, definitely made my face a little too tan. Make sure you apply all over your face/neck. I didn?™t blend into my eye lid area and it?™s obvious. column11: Orange Hands immediately after application-use glo

column10: I wanted to try this after I ran out of my tan luxe face drops. I noticed my forehead started breaking out really bad after a few uses. Also very blotchy. Then I tried mixing with my lotion to extend my tan and my entire body broke out into hives. I know everyone doesn?™t have sensitive skin, but if you do, be very careful using this!

Ok so I have gone through several bottles of the dark since last year. I was coming back to the self-tan stage after tanning at the gym I worked at for over a year..every day. At 31 I was ready to quit tanning. Admittedly I fudged the first application because what the heck is this product?! I recommend doing each part of your body in sections. A couple pumps of lotion and probably 3-4 drops for each arm, 2 drops for face, add extra for legs. Wash your hands after each section. When doing your arms, end with hands and gently wipe them with a soft cloth and do a little more lotion. Same for feet. Be careful when you are washing your hands, if water drips somewhere on you it can mess with the tan. Think of it like buildable foundation. Start light with a few drops, see how it looks, do a little the next day. It?™s the safest way to avoid the usual mishaps. I stay pale when I?™m not by the pool, but I prefer the dark because I have warm undertone and I feel like I need fewer drops of the dark to get where I wanna be. I did just purchase the value kit with the medium drops, half-size tanning water and mitt because it?™s a heck of a deal. I hope this helps at least one person!

column10: Before I start, I want to preface this by saying that I received a 7 day trial of this free from Influenster in exchange for an honest review. I agree with a lot of people who posted a review, having also tried a trial, that 7 days isn?™t quite long enough to really test out the benefits of this product. The description states that this product can be used morning and evening but because it was a daily trial, I only used this product at night - right after my toner and before the rest of my skin care routine. That being said, I?™ve really liked it so far and I think I would see a lot of benefit if I continued using this product in the future. I did a lot of research on this product prior to starting my trial so I would know what to look for in terms of benefits and drawbacks. SMELL & TEXTURE: I actually love the smell of this. It has hints of florals and I feel like I can smell a little bit of fruity scents like pear but I?™m not sure. Either way, the smell is just enough that it is extremely pleasant - definitely not overpowering. As for the texture, the double-serum part of the name comes from one pump of product being an oil-based formula while the other pump is a water-based formula. You mix the two together in order to get the benefits of both the water and oil. With my 7 day trial, I didn?™t feel as though the packaging had equal parts and the oil based part definitely overpowered the water. I generally use oils on my face as part of my skincare routine (jojoba and rosehip) so I knew what to expect but I can see how people who use this product that aren?™t familiar to oils might find it a bit heavy. However, for a oil-based product, it didn?™t feel too greasy and settled into my face pretty quickly after application.BENEFITS: After having done extensive research, I knew that this product was supposed to help with smoothing of fine lines and wrinkles, evening out texture and uneven skin tones, firming the skin, moisturizing, and helping the skin feel and look radiant. After my 7 days, I definitely noticed an improvement in firming the skin, moisturizing, and radiance. My skin felt more elastic and that allowed my makeup to look more smooth on my skin which I really appreciated. The oil also did a great job of keeping my skin moisturized and hydrated. I usually use a water based moisturizer and a heavy cream on top because I?™ve been having extremely dry spots around my nose and the lower sides of my mouth. When using this product, the dryness didn?™t go away completely but my skin did stop flaking - even if I didn?™t use a heavy cream on top.DRAWBACKS: Where I didn?™t notice much improvement was in the firming of fine lines and wrinkles as well as helping to even out my skin tone. I do have some fine lines around my eyes that I didn?™t see any noticeable improvements in. Also, I do have some problems with uneven skin tone around my lip corners as well as around my scars from pimples. I didn?™t see this product do much for that. The caveat is that I really only used this product for 7 days and these skin care issues usually take longer to combat so I can?™t really speak to that for sure!All in all, I would really consider using this double-serum long term as part of my daily skincare routine and would encourage anyone to try it out - especially if you could get your hands on a decently sized sample!

column10: Not to be confused with hyaluronic acid, this product contains sodium hyaluronate, which is the salt of hyaluronic acid. Sodium hyaluronate has a smaller molecular structure and can hold up to 1,000x its weight in water. It functions as a humectant, drawing water from the deeper layers of the skin up into the epidermis. However this product alone is NOT a moisturizer, it does not contain any occlusive agents. In order to use this effectively you need to put it on BEFORE using an actual moisturizer. The humectant properties of this serum will attract extra moisture and then adding an actual occlusive moisturizer on top will form a barrier to hold that moisture in. I find myself reaching for this a lot more now that it?™s winter and my skin is drier, thus needing the extra hydration. I?™m sure it would be great all year round for someone with dry skin, however, given the price, personally only like to use it when I need an extra moisture boost. Again, only truly effective when an actual moisturizer is used directly after putting this on. I wish they would include that info in the product description, because it seems a lot of people are trying to use it as a moisturizer alone and not seeing any benefit and that?™s why. When used correctly it?™s great. I don?™t blame people for not knowing though, it?™s their bad for not explaining how to properly use their product.
